look_here_first: Look at a mature leaf first: usually oblong to ovate, relatively broad, with a blunt, rounded or shortly acute tip. Then check the flower: five reddish-purple hoods form the corona, but there is no conspicuous projecting horn. Compare the relatively short corona segments with the much longer pale green corolla lobes; confirm against narrow, taper-tipped A. asperula.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Irregularly arranged, alternate to subopposite (occasionally opposite); do not treat apparently opposite leaves as a definitive identification character.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually broad oblong to ovate (sometimes lanceolate), approximately 1–6 cm wide; tip obtuse/rounded to shortly acute, entire margins sometimes gently wavy.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Crowded terminal umbel-like clusters; additional lateral umbels may occur at a few upper nodes. Both this species and A. asperula can make dense clusters, so cluster looseness alone is unreliable.

key_traits.label: Flower color
key_traits.text: Pale-green corolla lobes surrounding a corona with frequently rose to purplish-red hoods; colors vary.

key_traits.label: Gynostegium detail
key_traits.text: Five pouch-like corona hoods are present. They lack a clearly projecting horn; an incipient horn/rudiment may be visible within a hood pocket (UT Williamson County description). Corona segments are generally less than half the length of the pale-green corolla lobes (Flora of North America comparison).

key_traits.label: Growth habit
key_traits.text: Perennial with stems spreading or decumbent to ascending, sometimes upright, often to roughly 50–60 cm; habit alone overlaps with A. asperula.
